title: More Condors Now Fly Free Than Live In Captivity
source: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service California Condor Recovery Program population records: 1987 -- the last 27 wild condors were trapped into captivity, leaving zero in the wild; 1992 -- first captive-bred birds released (about 2 wild, 25 captive); 2010 -- total population 370 (181 wild-flying, 189 captive), per FWS-sourced population chart (ResearchGate fig. 3); 2020 -- total 504 (329 wild, 175 captive), FWS year-end status report; 2025 -- total 607 (approximately 350 wild-flying, 257 captive), FWS '2025 California Condor Population Status Report' (published Feb 2026).
